01.event: teaches a baraita before Rabbi Yohanan
01.outcome: tells him to go teach it outside
01.summary: Rabbi Zakkai recited a baraita before Rabbi Yohanan, who told him to go teach it outside, rejecting it.
01.missing: any event beyond teaching and a rebuke
01.reason: Only speech: a teaching and a dismissive retort, which is ordinary scholarly rebuke rather than conflict with change.

02.actor: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua
02.event: finds the Sages in Rav's study hall discussing halla
02.outcome: he states the opposite view with a proof
02.summary: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua found the Sages saying halla is Torah law today; he told them the opposite and brought a baraita.
02.reason: A setting plus a scholarly exchange of views; standard rabbinic dialogue without an event.

03.actor: a man in Mata Mehasya and his brother
03.event: a yevama falls to the man; his brother wants to disqualify her with a divorce
03.turn: the man offers to share the property; brother fears being swindled
03.outcome: the man offers to divide it immediately
03.summary: A man in Mata Mehasya became obligated to a yevama, and his brother wanted to disqualify her by a bill of divorce. The man offered to share the estate; the brother feared a swindle like the Pumbeditan's, so the man offered to divide it right away.
03.missing: what actually happened after the offer
03.reason: There is a real situation and a conflict, but it is carried almost entirely by dialogue and no outcome is narrated.

04.event: the man sells land to Rav Pappa to buy oxen
04.turn: he ends up not needing the money
04.summary: A man sold land to Rav Pappa because he needed money for oxen. In the end he did not need it, and Rav Pappa gave him back his land, beyond the letter of the law.
04.reason: An actual event with several actions and a change (sale, changed need, return of land), not a hypothetical, even though cited as a proof.

05.actor: the people of the Upper Galilee
05.event: buy a litra of meat daily for a poor man of noble descent
05.summary: The people of the Upper Galilee bought a poor man of good family from Tzippori a litra of meat every day; the Gemara then discusses what made this remarkable.
05.missing: any one-time event, response or consequence
05.reason: A report of a habitual practice that leads nowhere, followed by Gemara discussion.

06.event: betroths a woman with a handful of onions from the field
06.outcome: Rava rules the onions were not his, so the betrothal fails
06.summary: A sharecropper betrothed a woman with a handful of onions taken from the field he worked and came before Rava, who asked who had given him the onions, implying the betrothal was invalid.
06.reason: An actual incident with an act (taking onions and betrothing) followed by a ruling, but little change beyond the ruling; between borderline and not, borderline.

07.event: acts in a case of a bundle of branches
07.summary: The judges of Pumbedita report that Rav Yehuda decided an actual case involving a bundle of branches.
07.missing: the incident itself, which is only named
07.reason: An actual case is alluded to but not narrated; an incident only alluded to is borderline, preferred over not.

08.missing: any narrated event; it is a self-statement about marrying at sixteen
08.reason: A bare personal statement used as a teaching, with nothing happening.

09.outcome: he rules to complete the bill with a slave
09.summary: People came before Rabbi Ami about a bill of divorce lacking witnesses and he told them to complete it even with a slave.
09.missing: any event besides coming before the rabbi
09.reason: Coming before a rabbi and his ruling is the only event; not a story.

10.actor: Rabbi Tarfon, Rabbi Akiva and the Elders
10.event: reclining in the upper room in Lod, asked whether study or action is greater
10.outcome: all conclude study is greater because it leads to action
10.summary: Rabbi Tarfon and the Elders were reclining in the loft of Nit'za's house in Lod when asked whether study or action is greater. Tarfon said action, Akiva said study, and all agreed study is greater because it leads to action.
10.missing: any action beyond the setting and the debate
10.reason: A setting plus a dialogue; there is disagreement resolved by a collective decision, so mainly speech with some conflict and change, borderline rather than not.

11.reason: Pure speech, a dietary teaching attributed to Elijah, with no event or conflict.

12.event: has houses in five courtyards in Usha
12.turn: the case comes before the Sages
12.outcome: they rule only a residence prohibits
12.summary: Ben Nappaha owned houses in five courtyards in Usha; the case came before the Sages, who ruled that only a place of residence renders carrying prohibited.
12.missing: any action or change beyond the case coming to court
12.reason: A situation brought before rabbis and ruled on, with no other narrated action or change.

13.event: someone comes before Rav Yosef about a daughter's sustenance
13.outcome: Rav Yosef clarifies what he meant
13.summary: Someone came before Rav Yosef, who ordered the heirs to give the daughter sustenance from dates on the mats; Abaye objected and Rav Yosef explained he meant dates still attached.
13.missing: any action beyond the ruling and scholarly exchange
13.reason: A case before a rabbi, a ruling, and an ordinary scholarly challenge; nothing else happens.

14.event: the Sages report a dispute with attributions reversed to Rav Mordekhai
14.turn: he recalls Rav Ashi answering on the step
14.summary: The Sages sent a reversed report of a dispute to Rav Mordekhai, who replied by recalling how Rav Ashi, standing with one foot on the step, had ruled a child's gift valid.
14.missing: any event beyond transmitting and recalling rulings
14.reason: Transmission of teachings and a recalled question-and-answer; quasi-speech acts with no conflict beyond correcting a report.

15.missing: an actual event; the scenario is a hypothetical case posed by the Gemara
15.reason: A hypothetical legal case constructed in the give-and-take, not an event that happened.

16.event: she seizes a silver cup toward her ketubah and demands sustenance
16.outcome: Rava orders the orphans to give her sustenance
16.summary: A woman seized a silver cup as partial payment of her ketubah and also demanded sustenance; she came before Rava, who told the orphans to support her.
16.missing: whether the orphans complied or anything changed after the ruling
16.reason: There is an act before the ruling (seizing the cup), but otherwise it is an incident plus ruling with only implied outcome; between borderline and not, borderline.

17.actor: Rabbi Hanina Kara and Rabbi Yannai
17.event: Hanina states the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda
17.outcome: tells him to recite his verses outside
17.summary: Rabbi Hanina Kara sat before Rabbi Yannai and said the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda; Yannai told him to go recite his verses outside.
17.reason: A ruling and a sharp retort, which is ordinary Talmudic discourse, not conflict with change.

18.event: arrives at the house of bar Shafei Halla and examines them
18.summary: Rav visited the house of the son of a vinegar strainer and had them examined; the Gemara debates whether it was for lineage or their silence.
18.missing: what the examination found or led to
18.reason: An actual incident is only alluded to as evidence in the discussion, with no outcome; alluded incidents are borderline.

19.event: Ravina comes to Mehoza; his host shows him a slaughtering knife
19.turn: Ravina refuses to examine it himself
19.outcome: tells him to take it to Rava
19.summary: Ravina visited Mehoza, Rava's town, and his host brought him a slaughtering knife to inspect. Ravina told him to bring it to Rava instead.
19.missing: what happened after; the rest is the host's question and Ravina's answer
19.reason: A visit and a shown knife are real events, but the substance is an instruction and legal point; mainly speech with some event.

20.actor: the people of Nehardea and Rav Nahman
20.event: during a drought everyone sells their mansions to buy wheat
20.outcome: Rav Nahman rules the mansions return to their owners
20.summary: In a drought in Nehardea everyone sold their mansions to buy wheat. Then wheat arrived, and Rav Nahman ruled that the mansions revert to their owners.
20.reason: An actual incident with multiple events and a change of circumstance, resolved by a ruling that itself changes ownership.
